facts.fact: A feature writer is hired in steps: a treatment, a first draft screenplay, a second draft, then rewrites and polishes, each with its own minimum.
A WGA member may not begin any work, including reviewing stock film, before a definite assignment under contract.
Before a director is engaged on a theatrical film, a television pilot, a movie-of-the-week or a closed-end series, the company arranges a pre-production meeting between the producer and the writer.

When a director is assigned to a film from an existing screenplay, the director meets the currently employed writer before any decision to hire a new writer (a voluntary guideline, not a contract term).
Each participating writer of a theatrical film has the right to see a cut of the film during a Writer's Viewing Period, early enough that approved editing suggestions could be made.
The credited writers of a theatrical film are invited to the domestic premiere or the first domestic festival screening, with travel paid when it is more than 150 miles away.

In television, a development room is three or more writers convened before the company has a firm commitment for a season; it needs at least 3 writer-producers including the showrunner, and each writer is guaranteed at least 10 consecutive weeks.

After a season order the company must convene a writers' room unless one writer writes every episode; the room's minimum size is 3 writers for 1 to 6 episodes, 5 for 7 to 12, and 6 for 13 or more, at least 3 of them writer-producers.
Room writers are guaranteed at least 20 weeks or the whole post-greenlight room, whichever is shorter.

On single-camera HBSVOD and pay-TV series filmed in the US and Canada, the showrunner and 2 writer-producers must be employed through production for 20 weeks or the production period, whichever is shorter.

The kinds of covered work include theatrical films (high and low budget), network prime time and other television, pay and basic cable, high budget streaming (SVOD and AVOD), comedy-variety, quiz, daytime serials, documentary, news and other new media; videogames, informational programs and podcasts are covered by separate special agreements, and animation terms are negotiated case by case.
A streaming program counts as High Budget SVOD only at or above $1,030,000 for 20-35 minutes, $1,750,000 for 36-65 minutes and $3,000,000 for 66 minutes or more; under 20 minutes never counts.
Television staff writers are paid separately for formats, bibles, stories and teleplays on top of their weekly pay.
O*NET (US Department of Labor) puts Writers and Authors (27-3043.00) at 140,300 employed in 2025, with 11,900 projected openings for 2025-2035.

The WGA counts television writing jobs in three levels: lower (staff writer, story editor, executive story editor), mid (co-producer through consulting or supervising producer) and upper (co-executive producer through showrunner).

The titles in the WGA's own order are Staff Writer, Story Editor, Executive Story Editor, Co-Producer, Producer, Supervising Producer, Consulting Producer, Co-Executive Producer, Executive Producer, Showrunner.
In the 2023-24 season there were 1,819 WGA television series writing jobs on 228 covered series, down from 3,138 jobs on 362 series in 2022-23.
The MBA has distinct weekly minimums by rung: staff writer, story editor and executive story editor, and writer-producer (co-producer and above).

A writer becomes a "professional writer" under the MBA after 13 weeks (not necessarily consecutive) of employment as a film, TV or dramatic radio writer, or one screen credit, or credit for one professionally produced stage play or one published novel, among other routes.

The Academy's Writers Branch considers a writer with at least two theatrical feature credits, or an Academy writing nomination, or a writing credit on a Best Picture, International Feature or Animated Feature nominee.

The Disney Entertainment Television Writing Program is a 12-month program aiming to staff its writers on Disney series as staff writers, without guarantee; writers are company employees on a non-negotiable weekly salary and must write at least one original pilot.
The Disney program's 2027 application window ran May 4 to June 1, 2026; it asks for two original live-action pilot scripts, a resume, an essay and a staffing pitch.

The Academy Nicholl Fellowships award up to five $35,000 fellowships a year to writers whose lifetime film and TV writing earnings do not exceed $25,000; the 2024 entry fee was $50 to $120 by deadline, for one feature script of 70 to 160 pages.
Of the 5,599 Nicholl entries in 2023, about 5% reached the quarterfinals, about 2% the semifinals and about 10 to 15 the finals.
A WGA member may sign only with an agency franchised by the Guild.
A franchised agency's commission is capped at 10% of the writer's gross compensation, including profit participation, with no commission on residuals or other reuse minimums.
Agencies lost the right to packaging fees on June 30, 2022, and an agency and its owners may not own more than 20% of a production or distribution entity.
A representation agreement under Rider W runs at most two years, and the writer may end it if no bona fide offer of covered work comes for more than six consecutive months.

In California anyone who procures work for a writer must hold a talent agency licence from the Labor Commissioner: a $25 filing fee, a $225 annual licence fee and a $50,000 surety bond; an unlicensed person may only negotiate alongside a licensed agency at its request.
A WGA member may not write on speculation for a producer, or under any deal whose payment depends on approval or the producer's ability to pay.
A writer can register a script with the WGA West Registry for $20 ($10 for members), valid five years and renewable.
A graduate route: Northwestern's MFA in Writing for the Screen and Stage requires 18 units over two years and a final portfolio of at least three substantial scripts.
The 2026 MBA runs May 2, 2026 to May 1, 2030; most minimums rose 1.5% in the first year and rise 3% on each of May 2, 2027, 2028 and 2029.
A high budget feature is one costing $5,000,000 or more; a low budget feature costs less.

High budget theatrical minimums for May 2, 2026 to May 1, 2027: original screenplay including treatment $173,215 (treatment $69,228, first draft $69,228, second draft $34,759); non-original including treatment $150,139; rewrite $46,152; polish $23,077; page-one rewrite $57,500.
Low budget theatrical minimums for the same year: original screenplay including treatment $92,268; rewrite $30,273; polish $15,148; page-one rewrite $31,500.
A writer hired for a first draft (or whose screenplay is bought) at 225% of minimum or less must also be hired for a rewrite at no less than the rewrite minimum.
Theatrical week-to-week minimums: $7,511 week-to-week, $6,970 a week on 14 of 14 weeks, $6,436 on 20 of 26, $5,925 on 40 of 52.

Network prime time story and teleplay minimums (also Tier 1 streaming): $17,631 for 15 minutes or less, $32,270 for 30 minutes, $47,460 for 60 minutes; a pilot is 150% and a back-up script 115% of these.
Television staff writer minimums: $6,024 a week week-to-week or on 6 of 6 weeks, $5,597 on 14 of 14, $5,164 on 20 of 26, $4,720 on 40 of 52.

Story editors and executive story editors earn at least $11,233 a week (up to 9 weeks), writer-producers (co-producer and above) at least $12,304 a week (up to 9 weeks), $10,254 (10 to 19 weeks) or $9,223 (20 weeks or more).
Development room weekly minimums (up to 19 weeks): staff writer $7,530, story editor or executive story editor $14,043, writer-producer $15,379.

An episodic fee may be spread over no more than 2.4 weeks of work on short seasons (14 or fewer episodes for streaming and basic cable, 12 or fewer for broadcast), unless the writer earns at least $450,000 in episodic fees for the season ($475,000 for contracts from May 2, 2027; $375,000 for basic cable and HB AVOD).
Network prime time episodic series pay program fees: $1,266 per 30-minute episode, at most 3 fees per episode split among eligible writers.
A series format pays at least $20,000.
Theatrical residuals: 1.2% of distributor's gross for TV, cable and streaming reuse, none for the theatrical release, and 1.5% then 1.8% of producer's gross on discs.

A network prime time rerun of a 15-minute-or-less episode pays $7,523 to the story-and-teleplay writer; other reruns pay a falling share of the residual base, from 40% (50% on a network) for the second run down to 5% from the thirteenth.

High budget streaming residuals after the first 90 days are the residual base times an exhibition-year percentage (45% in year 1, 40%, 35%, 25%, 20%, 15%, 10%, 10%, 10%, 5%, 5%, 5%, then 1.5%) times a subscriber factor (65% under 20 million, 100% for 20 to 45 million, 150% over 45 million).

A high budget streaming season that is watched by 20% or more of the service's domestic subscribers in its first 90 days pays a bonus of 50% of the fixed residual, 75% for programs first shown from January 1, 2027.
A writer with only "Teleplay by" credit and no "Story by" credit gets 100% of the fixed residual under the 2026 MBA.

Flat-deal steps at twice minimum or less are paid 50% on commencement, another 25% if not delivered within 9 weeks, and the last 25% on delivery; payment is due within 7 days of delivery, with 1.5% a month interest if late.
A script publication fee of $12,500 in aggregate goes to the credited writers within 30 days of final credits.
O*NET reports a 2025 median wage of $76,910 a year ($36.98 an hour) for Writers and Authors, from BLS data.

In 2023, 1,918 WGAW writers reported $373 million in screen earnings, 4,441 reported television and digital earnings totalling $916.6 million, and 5,501 reported $1.29 billion in all; writer-producers report weekly pay at the Article 14 minimum, so overscale TV pay is not captured.

Current membership in the WGA West needs 24 units within the three years before application and a $2,500 initiation fee; fewer than 24 units gives Associate membership at $100 a year for up to three years.

Units: 2 per complete week of week-to-week employment; 24 for a feature screenplay or a teleplay of 90 minutes or more; 12 for a feature story; 8 for a 30-to-60-minute teleplay; a rewrite earns half and a polish a quarter of the category's units.
Work for the writer's own company, or written while the writer is a producer or performer on the project, counts toward membership only if the script is produced with an on-screen writing credit.
Current members pay quarterly dues of 1.5% of gross writing earnings plus $25, declared each quarter; producing and directing pay is not declared; a late declaration costs $10.
Employers contribute 11.25% of covered pay to the WGA pension plan (9.75% for pilots and first seasons), 16.25% to the health fund (16.75% from May 2, 2027) and 0.25% to the paid parental fund.

Health coverage for a year needs $47,460 in covered earnings within 4 or fewer quarters (from July 1, 2026), followed by a lag quarter; the threshold becomes 110% of the one-hour network prime time story-and-teleplay minimum ($53,773) in July 2027.

From January 1, 2027 active participants pay health premiums of $75 a month single, $150 with one dependent, $200 with more (Anthem PPO); extended coverage points are earned from $200,000 in annual earnings and spent at 4 a quarter.
A writer is generally vested in the pension plan after five qualified years of service, which need not be consecutive.

Working rules: no work for non-signatory companies (fine up to 100% of the pay), no ghost writing, no speculative work, every contract filed with the Guild within a week, and any producing or directing engagement reported to the Guild.
The 2023 WGA strike lasted 148 days; the 2023 MBA that ended it took effect September 25, 2023, and the 2026 MBA was agreed on April 4, 2026.

Screen writing credits are "Written by" (story and screenplay), "Story by", "Screen Story by", "Screenplay by", "Adaptation by" (only by arbitration), "Narration Written by" and "Based on Characters Created by".
An ampersand joins a writing team; "and" means the writers worked separately; a team of more than three needs a Guild waiver.
Story credit is shared by at most two writers, and screenplay credit by at most two except, through arbitration, three.

On an original screenplay the first writer needs more than 33% of the final shooting script for screenplay credit, a later writer 50%, and a later writer who is a producer or director more than 50%; on a non-original screenplay anyone needs more than 33%.

The company sends a Notice of Tentative Writing Credits and holds credits open at least 12 business days for protest; a contested credit goes to three anonymous arbiters and must be decided within 21 business days.
A writer paid less than $200,000 on a film may take a pseudonym within 5 business days of final credits; withdrawing from credit forfeits every right that comes with it.

In television, the first teleplay writer keeps at least shared credit unless a later writer contributes all four elements (construction, scenes, characterization, dialogue) so as to essentially eliminate the first writer's work.

The writer with separated rights in a series gets "Created by" credit on every episode and sequel payments; shares are at least 30% each in 10% steps; "Developed by" goes to a writer who added distinctiveness but not enough for "Created by".
The Academy gives two writing awards, Adapted Screenplay and Original Screenplay; the screenplay must be human-authored with an explicit screenwriting credit.
Writers Branch members nominate by preferential ballot of up to five per category, the top five become nominees, and all active and life Academy members vote the winner.

For the 99th Oscars a film needs a theatrical qualifying run beginning between January 1 and December 31, 2026, of at least seven consecutive days in one commercial theatre in a qualifying US metro area.

WGA screenplay awards require a WGA (or affiliate guild) contract, a final credit determination and at least one week's theatrical exhibition in Los Angeles or New York in 2026; financial-core non-members are ineligible.

Emmy writing awards go to writers credited "written by", "teleplay by" or "story by"; in comedy and drama series an entrant needs at least a 50% credit share, with teleplay counting 60% and story 40%.
The 78th Emmys covered programs shown June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026; an individual entry costs a $125 processing charge plus $100 per entrant.

In television a writer also employed as executive producer, producer, associate producer, story editor or executive story editor is a "writer also employed in additional capacities", employed as a writer at least as long as in the other role and only week-to-week or on term.
A writer-producer's writing pay must be stated separately and be at least the Article 14 minimum; producing pay cannot be offset against writing pay.

A director (or producer) hired without writing duties may change dialogue, narration or action without MBA coverage, but significant changes to plot, story line or character relationships bring the work under the MBA.

Any producing or directing credit makes a writer a "production executive" for credits: such a writer needs more than 50% of an original screenplay as a later writer, and their proposed credit always goes to arbitration when other writers are involved.
A production executive claiming team credit with another writer must notify the Guild and that writer in writing when the team work begins.
A "production" or "presentation" credit is exempt from the MBA's advertising limits when its holder is the writer-director, writer-producer or writer-director-producer and the sole credited writer.
A member must report any engagement as producer, director or executive to the Guild, and earnings from producing or directing are not subject to WGA dues.

topics.topic: Time and money of a project

facts.fact: A contract or deal memo is due generally within 10 to 12 days of agreeing the main deal points.

A theatrical option on a professional writer's material runs up to 18 months for at least 10% of minimum, each renewal another 18 months for another 10%; a television option runs 180 days for 5% of minimum, then 10% per further 180 days.
From January 1, 2027 an if/come pilot deal leaves the writer non-exclusive until the first writing step is paid.
Streaming initial pay covers 90 days of worldwide use on the original platform before residuals begin.
A WGA script registration lasts five years.
In 2024 women were 32.6% of employed screenwriters and men 66.4%.
In the 2023-24 season women were 45.0% of television series writers and men 52.5%.

Women's share falls up the television ladder: showrunners in 2023-24 were 8.1% BIPOC women and 18.5% White women against 6.5% BIPOC men and 46.2% White men, while staff writers were 32.4% BIPOC women and 15.7% White women.
Writers 55 and over held 21.6% of screen employment in 2024 (16.1% in 2020) and 15.3% of series employment in 2023-24 (11.7% in 2020-21).

The Academy Gold Fellowship for Women is open to alumni of Academy Gold programs who identify as women and to Gold Rising partner nominees; two are awarded a year, one US and one international, for a one-year program.
Nicholl entrants must be 18 or older when they enter.
Disney's writing program requires applicants to be at least 21 by December 1 of the application year and legally able to work in the US.
A minor's contract for creative services, expressly including a writer's, with a licensed talent agency cannot be disaffirmed if the superior court approved it.

Under California Family Code 6752 the court approving a minor's entertainment contract orders 15% of gross earnings set aside in trust by the employer, and 15% is set aside even when the contract is not taken to court.

Readings made: 'agreed on April 4, 2026' is the MOA's date line; the 2023 strike's 148 days is the annual report's phrase, and its start and end dates were not read on a WGA page; the TV title order is the order of the Inclusion Report's Table 10 rows, and the three levels are the Snapshot's grouping; the showrunner shares by sex are the Table 10 cells as printed, not summed; 'two years' for the Northwestern MFA is the catalog's 'Required in 1st and 2nd year'; the description of feature steps as the work's sequence is the order of the Schedule of Minimums' installments.
